name: ZipCache: Accurate and Efficient KV Cache Quantization with Salient Token Identification
problem: Adaptive KV compression that picks salient tokens degrades sharply at high compression ratios because salient-token identification is inaccurate.
mechanism: Two parts: (1) a strong quantization BASELINE via CHANNEL-SEPARABLE TOKENWISE quantization - token-wise (not fine-grained group-wise) scales so the scale metadata overhead is far smaller, which is what makes high compression ratios reachable at all; (2) NORMALIZED ATTENTION SCORE as the saliency metric, exploiting the LOWER-TRIANGLE structure of the causal attention matrix, plus an efficient approximation that decouples the scoring from the full attention computation.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): prior adaptive approaches 'exhibit significant performance degradation at high compression ratios due to inaccuracies in identifying salient tokens'; ZipCache fixes this with the channel-separable tokenwise scheme and normalized attention score. COMPRESSION RATIO: adaptive/mixed-precision KV (not a fixed bit width - salient tokens keep higher precision), so no single ratio applies. QUALITY COST: no paired accuracy delta in the abstract, so speedup_reported states the qualitative claim only.
